background.title: Background Information
background.subtitle: The following questions help us determine eligibility for Food Assistance and other programs. All information is kept confidential.

questions.drugFelony: Has anyone in your household been convicted of a drug-related felony after August 22, 1996?
questions.tradingBenefits: Has anyone in your household been convicted of trading SNAP benefits for drugs, weapons, or explosives?
questions.fleeingProsecution: Is anyone in your household currently fleeing to avoid prosecution or custody for a felony?
questions.fraudDisqualification: Has anyone in your household been subject to a fraud disqualification for SNAP or FIP?
questions.abawd: Is anyone in your household between ages 18–49, without dependents, and physically able to work?
questions.otherStateBenefits: Has anyone in your household received SNAP benefits in another state in the last 12 months?
questions.childSupportDisqualification: Has anyone in your household been disqualified from FIP for refusing to cooperate with child support?

background.infoTooltip: This question is required by federal and state regulations. Your answer helps determine program eligibility.

rightsResponsibilities.title: Rights & Responsibilities

rights.apply: You have the right to apply for assistance. We will help you with your application. You may have someone help you. We will tell you what we need to decide if you can get assistance.
rights.dignity: You have the right to be treated with dignity and respect, without regard to race, creed, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, religion, age, or disability.
rights.fairHearing: You have the right to a fair hearing if you think we have made a wrong decision about your case. You must ask for a hearing within 90 days from the date of the notice of decision.
rights.withdraw: You have the right to withdraw your application at any time before we make a decision. To withdraw, you must tell us in writing or come to the office and tell us you want to withdraw.
rights.caseRecord: You have the right to see your case record. You may see any information in the file that affects your case. Some information may be kept from you when the law says we must keep it confidential.
rights.confidentiality: You have the right to confidentiality. We will not give information from your case file to anyone unless the law allows it. If you want us to give information to someone, you must tell us in writing who can get information from your file.

responsibilities.truthful: You must give us complete and truthful information. You must prove your answers are true when we ask you to. You must tell us about any changes in your situation within 10 days.
responsibilities.cooperate: You must cooperate with quality control reviewers, investigators, and other people who check on the assistance you receive.
responsibilities.useBenefits: You must use your benefits as the program rules require. You must repay any assistance you get that you should not have gotten.
responsibilities.followRules: You must follow all program rules. If you do not follow the rules, you may have to repay benefits, your assistance may be reduced or stopped, and you may be prosecuted.
responsibilities.allowVerification: You must allow us to get information about you from other agencies, employers, and other sources to verify your eligibility.
responsibilities.snapReporting: For SNAP (Food Assistance): You must report if the total gross monthly income of all household members goes over the limit for your household size. You must report this within 10 days of the date you become aware of the change.
responsibilities.fipParticipation: For FIP (Family Investment Program): You must follow participation requirements, including work requirements, job search, and other activities we assign to you.

penalties.falseStatement: If you intentionally make a false statement or misrepresent facts to get or continue to get benefits, you may be subject to criminal prosecution and civil penalties. You may also be disqualified from receiving benefits for a period of time.
penalties.disqualificationSchedule: First violation: 12 months disqualification. Second violation: 24 months disqualification. Third violation: Permanent disqualification.

rightsResponsibilities.consentText: By signing this application, you consent to the State-X Department of Health and Human Services accessing information about you and your household from various sources including but not limited to: wage and employment verification systems, financial institutions, utility companies, other state and federal agencies, and third-party data verification services. This information will be used solely for the purpose of determining and verifying your eligibility for assistance programs.

I have consent for all people I will list on the application that allows their information to be retrieved and used from data sources for this application.

snapScreening.title: Food Assistance — Quick Check
snapScreening.subtitle: We'll ask a few quick questions to see if your household might qualify for faster processing.

questions.grossIncome: Is your household's total gross income this month under $150?
questions.cashResources: Does your household have less than $100 in cash, checking, or savings?
questions.shelterCosts: Are your monthly shelter and utility costs more than your income and resources combined?
questions.farmWorker: Is anyone in your household a migrant or seasonal farm worker?

fasterProcessing.title: You may qualify for faster processing!
fasterProcessing.description: A worker will contact you within 7 days of your application to begin processing your food assistance.
